question: Summarize the curated literature on whether zebrafish have a histologically distinct corneal endothelium, and grade the evidence.
direct_answer:
The retrieved evidence bundle does NOT contain any curated histological, anatomical, or morphological literature that directly addresses whether zebrafish possess a histologically distinct corneal endothelium. I therefore cannot substantiate an answer from the provided material, and any conclusion would be unsupported speculation.

What the bundle does contain (and its limits): (1) CORPUS-2026-0001 (ZESTA) and CORPUS-2026-0002 are transcriptomic atlases. CORPUS-2026-0001 covers the 3–24 hpf *pre-corneal* window — i.e., before the cornea has formed — so it cannot speak to a differentiated corneal endothelium. CORPUS-2026-0002 is a scRNA atlas of anterior-segment development (trabecular meshwork / annular ligament) described as closing a 'cornea' gap, and is the single most relevant item; however, the snippet provides no histological or endothelial-layer findings, only that it profiles anterior-segment tissues. (3) CORPUS-2026-0003 concerns pronephros tubulogenesis (irrelevant to cornea). DanioCODE, Reactome, and niche RN10 are regulatory/pathway/tissue-boundary resources, not corneal histology sources. No Path B external literature was triggered.

In short: the corneal-relevant evidence here is exclusively molecular/transcriptomic (single-cell atlases), with no curated histology. The question — a histological/anatomical one about the presence of a distinct endothelial layer — is not answerable from this bundle. To answer it properly you would need histological/EM literature on the zebrafish cornea (classically, the mammalian corneal endothelium is a single posterior cell layer; whether teleost/zebrafish corneas have a homologous distinct endothelium versus a simpler stromal/Descemet-like arrangement requires primary morphological studies not present here).
